chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When the woman says to her husband the sentence, 'I will not obey you in a matter,' whether it is specified or not specified, it is permissible for him what he takes from her, and there is no return (revocation of divorce) for him upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence for a husband if his wife declares she will not obey him in the context of Khul'a?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal consequences of a wife's explicit declaration of disobedience (Nushuz), establishing that the husband retains the Khul'a compensation and loses the right of unilateral revocation (Raj'ah). This ruling underscores the irrevocability of the divorce in this specific context, requiring a new marriage contract (Iqad) if the couple wishes to reunite, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital stability and financial equity. The hadith highlights the seriousness of the wife's voluntary assertion of her right to separate, thereby finalizing the dissolution of the marital bond without the need for further judicial intervention regarding the compensation.
